newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Speculative dlr buying pushes won to record low.
newsitem.headline: Speculative dlr buying pushes won to record low.

text.p: The South Korean won ended at new 84-month low against the U.S. currency on Monday on speculative dollar buying, dealers said.

They attributed the plunge to the widening current account deficit and the dollar's strength on world markets. They added that rising inter-Korean tension was only minor factor in the day's won/dollar movement.
The won ended at 880.00 after opening at 876.70. This is the lowest level seen since the market average system was introduced in March 1990.
The won touched a high of 875.00
South Korea posted a record current account deficit of $23.72 billion in 1996, compared to a shortfall of $8.95 billion in 1995, the central bank figures showed.
"Players are convinced the dollar will continue to rise, so they are speculatively buying the unit," said a western bank dealer.

The central bank stepped into the market early in the day to sell dollars, but the half-hearted intervention failed to prevent the won from falling further. The central bank has refused to confirm or deny that it intervenes in the interbank market.
"I think the BOK is saving up its ammunition for one major intervention that will be more effective," a local dealer said.
Dealers said they expected the won to move in a 880-883 range on Tuesday. Tuesday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 878.80 against 875.00 today.

The shooting of prominent defector Li Il-nam on Saturday by suspected North Korean agents triggered fears of growing tension on the Korean peninsula. The shooting appeared to be a warning to Seoul and potential asylum seekers after a high-ranking Pyongyang official sought political asylum at the South Korean embassy in Beijing last week. -- Katherine Bruce 727 5644
